proofs.proof_tex:
Put
\[
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\]
By \(k\geq2\), \(m\geq1\), and \(n\geq2\), one has \(q>0\). The hypotheses on independent environment sampling and the tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), together with the regularity conditions inherited from the model class and the certified estimator construction, permit application of \(\mathrm{lem:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}law\text{-}recovery}\). Consequently,
\[
\lim_{M\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)}
\Pr_\theta\!\left\{D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)>M\rho_N\right\}=0.
\tag{1}
\]
This is precisely the first asserted uniform stochastic order.

We next transfer (1) to the representation discrepancy. Since the estimator is constrained by \(\mathrm{def:certified\text{-}spectral\text{-}estimator}\) to take values in the same model class as \(\theta\), \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\) supplies a class-uniform constant \(C_R<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathcal E(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
\leq C_R D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N).
\tag{2}
\]
The permutation in (2) is the optimizing common group alignment required by \(\mathrm{def:analytic\text{-}residual}\). Whenever
\[
D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)\leq C_R^{-1},
\tag{3}
\]
equation (2) gives \(\mathcal E(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)\leq1\). Thus \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\), applied with that same alignment, yields a class-uniform constant \(C_W<\infty\) for which
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
&\leq C_W\mathcal E(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)^q\\
&\leq C_W C_R^qD_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)^q.
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]
No converse implication from vanishing representation discrepancy is used.

Let \(C_*=C_WC_R^q\). Since \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=k-1>0\), the definition
\[
\rho_N=(N/\log N)^{-s_{\mathrm{obs}}/(2s_{\mathrm{obs}}+n)}
\]
implies \(\rho_N\to0\). Fix \(M>0\). For all sufficiently large \(N\), \(M\rho_N\leq C_R^{-1}\), so (4) implies the event inclusion
\[
\left\{d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)>C_*M^q\rho_N^q\right\}
\subseteq
\left\{D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)>M\rho_N\right\}.
\tag{5}
\]
Taking the supremum over the model class, then \(\limsup_{N\to\infty}\), and finally \(M\to\infty\), equations (1) and (5) give
\[
\lim_{B\to\infty}\limsup_{N\to\infty}
\sup_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)}
\Pr_\theta\!\left\{
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)>B\rho_N^q
\right\}=0,
\]
because \(B=C_*M^q\to\infty\). This is the second asserted uniform stochastic order.

Finally, if \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), then \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=1\) and
\[
\rho_N=(N/\log N)^{-1/(2+2)}=(N/\log N)^{-1/4},
\qquad
q=\frac{2}{(2+2/2)(1+1)}=\frac13.
\]
Therefore
\[
\rho_N^q=(N/\log N)^{-1/12},
\]
which proves the primary-case rate.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Under independent sampling and for certified tolerance \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), the positive Fourier minimum-distance estimator satisfies
\[
D_H(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)=O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N)
\quad\text{and}\quad
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\theta,\widehat\theta_N)
=O_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{\rho_N^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\right\},
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal M_{n,k,m}(c_0,C_0,K,a_0,J,\Delta_0)\). In the primary case \(n=2\), \(k=2\), and \(m=1\), the representation rate is \((N/\log N)^{-1/12}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The frozen target's sharper representation exponent is not implied by its declared full-class dependencies. The established residual reduction and scalar finite-type weak-rigidity lemma yield the conservative full-class exponent, while the sharper exponent remains available only on the separately treated radial subclass or after resolving full incompressible rigidity. In the primary case this changes the unsupported sampling exponent to the proved one-twelfth exponent.

proofs.proof_tex:
The coverage assertion is exactly Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:corrected\text{-}confidence\text{-}coverage}\), whose assumptions include independent sampling in every environment.  It remains to control the displayed diameter.

Set
\[
r_N=2c_\alpha\rho_N+2\delta_N
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
q=\frac{k}{(k+n/2)(m+1)}.
\tag{1}
\]
We first verify the triangle inequality needed below directly from Definition \(\mathrm{def:full\text{-}law\text{-}distance}\).  For three models \(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_2,\vartheta_3\), let \(\pi\) and \(\sigma\) minimize the finite permutation criteria for the first--second and second--third pairs, respectively.  The Hellinger distance is a metric because it is, up to the constant factor \(2^{-1/2}\), the \(L^2(\lambda^n)\)-distance between square-root densities.  Thus, for the observational component and every \(i\in[n]\), \(e\in\{0,1\}\),
\[
H(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{obs}},P_{\vartheta_3}^{\mathrm{obs}})
\le
H(P_{\vartheta_1}^{\mathrm{obs}},P_{\vartheta_2}^{\mathrm{obs}})
+H(P_{\vartheta_2}^{\mathrm{obs}},P_{\vartheta_3}^{\mathrm{obs}}),
\tag{2}
\]
and
\[
H(P_{\vartheta_1}^{i,e},P_{\vartheta_3}^{\sigma(\pi(i)),e})
\le
H(P_{\vartheta_1}^{i,e},P_{\vartheta_2}^{\pi(i),e})
+H(P_{\vartheta_2}^{\pi(i),e},P_{\vartheta_3}^{\sigma(\pi(i)),e}).
\tag{3}
\]
Applying the Euclidean Minkowski inequality to the observational coordinate and the \(2n\) intervention coordinates in (2)--(3), and reindexing the second intervention sum by \(j=\pi(i)\), gives
\[
D_H(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_3)
\le D_H(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_2)+D_H(\vartheta_2,\vartheta_3),
\tag{4}
\]
because \(\sigma\circ\pi\in\mathfrak S_n\) is admissible for the first--third criterion.  The same definition also gives symmetry: replacing a permutation by its inverse and reindexing the intervention sum shows
\[
D_H(\vartheta_1,\vartheta_2)=D_H(\vartheta_2,\vartheta_1).
\tag{5}
\]

Now fix any two representing models \(\vartheta,\vartheta'\) occurring in the diameter.  Their defining constraints, (4), and (5) imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
D_H(\vartheta,\vartheta')
&\le D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)
   +D_H(\widehat\theta_N,\vartheta')\\
&=D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)
   +D_H(\vartheta',\widehat\theta_N)\\
&\le 2r_N
=4c_\alpha\rho_N+4\delta_N.
\end{aligned}
\tag{6}
\]
By \(k\ge2\), the definition \(s_{\mathrm{obs}}=k-1\), and the definition of \(\rho_N\), one has \(\rho_N\to0\).  Since \(\delta_N=o(\rho_N)\), equation (6) is uniformly \(O(\rho_N)\).

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:full\text{-}law\text{-}residual\text{-}reduction}\), applied with an optimizing common group permutation, supplies a class-uniform constant \(C_{\mathrm{red}}<\infty\) such that
\[
\mathcal E(\vartheta,\vartheta')
\le C_{\mathrm{red}}D_H(\vartheta,\vartheta')
\le 2C_{\mathrm{red}}r_N.
\tag{7}
\]
The right-hand side tends to zero, so it is at most one for all sufficiently large \(N\).  Lemma \(\mathrm{lem:scalar\text{-}finite\text{-}type\text{-}weak\text{-}rigidity}\) is therefore applicable to the same aligned pair.  Combining it with (7) yields, for a class-uniform constant \(C_{\mathrm{rig}}<\infty\),
\[
\begin{aligned}
d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\vartheta,\vartheta')
&\le C_{\mathrm{rig}}\mathcal E(\vartheta,\vartheta')^q\\
&\le C_{\mathrm{rig}}(2C_{\mathrm{red}}r_N)^q
=O\!\left(\rho_N^q\right).
\end{aligned}
\tag{8}
\]
All constants in (8) are uniform over the two models.  Consequently, taking the supremum over every representing pair in the confidence set preserves (8).  In fact the bound is deterministic for every realized center \(\widehat\theta_N\) once \(N\) is sufficiently large, and hence it implies the asserted \(O_{\mathbb P}(\rho_N^q)\) diameter bound.

Finally, if \((n,k,m)=(2,2,1)\), then
\[
q=\frac{2}{(2+2/2)(1+1)}=\frac13,
\qquad
s_{\mathrm{obs}}=1,
\qquad
\rho_N=(N/\log N)^{-1/4}.
\]
Therefore \(\rho_N^q=(N/\log N)^{-1/12}\), which proves the final specialization.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
For every fixed known \( (k,m) \) and \( \alpha\in(0,1) \), the corrected inverted set is uniformly honest,
\[
\inf_{\theta\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m}}
\Pr_\theta\{[h_\theta]\in\mathcal C_N(\alpha)\}
\ge 1-\alpha-o(1).
\]
Define its representing-model diameter by
\[
\sup\left\{d_{\mathrm{rep}}(\vartheta,\vartheta'):
\vartheta,\vartheta'\in\mathcal M_{n,k,m},\
D_H(\vartheta,\widehat\theta_N)\vee
D_H(\vartheta',\widehat\theta_N)
\le 2c_\alpha\rho_N+2\delta_N\right\}.
\]
This diameter is
\[
O_{\mathbb P}\!\left\{\rho_N^{k/((k+n/2)(m+1))}\right\}.
\]
In the primary case \( (n,k,m)=(2,2,1) \), this is
\(O_{\mathbb P}\{(N/\log N)^{-1/12}\}\).
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current diameter exponent is the conjectural sharp full-class rate, whereas the declared scalar weak-rigidity lemma proves only the smaller conservative exponent. The triangle inequality and full-law residual reduction preserve that conservative exponent, so the displayed rate must be narrowed.
